note: 1A3c, LOCOMOTIVE TRACTION ONLY under the re-based reference: the Year Book detail table splits locomotive from other-than-locomotive fuel, and the measured non-traction share books at its own category below. From Pakistan Railways Year Book metered fuel consumption. The mainline network has been diesel-only since about 2010 (electric energy NIL from the 2010-2015 quinquennium), so there is no scope-2 stream in the inventory years; urban electric rail is outside the operator and accounted under power.

Workshops, power houses, pumps and track machinery, measured by the Year Book detail table and booked at its own category since rc11 - by IPCC definition this fuel belongs in 1.A.2 / 1.A.4.c BY USE, and the source publishes no per-use split, which the category name declares. Rail factors retained (no use-specific factor is supportable), so the module total is conserved exactly against the pre-rc11 booking.
the conserved sector total: traction plus non-traction equals the summary fuel account's emissions to the last digit

category: Diagnostic: N2O on the road factor
note: What this sector would report if IPCC Table 3.2.2 (road, 3.9 kg N2O/TJ) were used instead of Table 3.4.1 (rail, 28.6). The gap is the reason the table choice is pinned by a test.

PERCENT, not Mt: the fraction of railway diesel burnt by workshops, power houses, pumps and track machines rather than by locomotives, from the detail table (since the 2024-25 restatement the detail and summary denominators agree to one part in 132,588). This sector used to call that split unobtainable. By IPCC definition the fuel belongs outside 1A3c - track machinery in off-road transport, workshops and power houses in stationary combustion, pumps by end use - not as a single block in 1A4c ii. Since rc11 it is BOOKED AT ITS OWN CATEGORY (1A2/1A4c unresolved) rather than left in 1A3c; only the final end-use split awaits the source.

kt of diesel, not Mt CO2e: the operator's own metered traction fuel, published for comparison against the petroleum industry's Railways customer-class total. Transport no longer deducts it - Railways is outside the Road customer class by construction - so this is an independent cross-source check, not an internal correction.

Mt CO2e by the identical method for series year 2018 (fiscal 2017-18), the inventory year BUR-1 reports as 4.06 Mt. The matched-year ratio is 8.7. This is the primary benchmark; the reference-year figure differs from the BUR's year by fuel (18 percent), not by method.
